name: Beriah
overview: Beriah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Elpaal according to 1 Chronicles 8:13. There are no additional notes or unique descriptors about his life or character beyond this genealogical placement. His mention situates him within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin.
namesAndTitles: The name Beriah means 'prominent' or 'excellent,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin as noted in 1 Chronicles 8:13. This meaning may indicate a family expectation or recognition of distinction, although the name was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Beriah as the son of Elpaal. Inferred relationships suggest that Beriah was also the father of Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, Michael, Ishpah, and Joha, as indicated in subsequent verses of 1 Chronicles 8. These connections place him within a broader family line within the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Beriah's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, which are important for tracing the lineage and heritage of God's people. His inclusion helps preserve the continuity of the tribe's ancestry, which is foundational for understanding the biblical narrative of God's covenant people. Though not a figure of major narrative action, his genealogical presence supports the biblical emphasis on God's providential care through generations.
